title: ICSE CLASS 2 — Environmental Studies | Biodiversity
description: Subject-wise test on Biodiversity (Environmental Studies) for ICSE CLASS 2. 25Q.
subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which of these is a very tall plant with a thick, woody stem called a trunk?

options.explanation: Herbs are small, non-woody plants.
Shrubs are smaller than trees and have multiple stems.
Trees are characterized by their tall height and a strong, woody stem known as a trunk.
Creepers have weak stems and grow along the ground.

questions.explanation: Trees are characterized by their tall height and a strong, woody stem known as a trunk.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which animal lives in a jungle and finds its own food without human help?

options.explanation: Cows are domestic animals.
Dogs are domestic animals.
A tiger is a wild animal that lives independently in jungles and hunts for its own food.
Hens are domestic animals.

questions.explanation: A tiger is a wild animal that lives independently in jungles and hunts for its own food.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Riya saw a plant growing along the ground with a very weak stem. What type of plant did she most likely see?

options.explanation: Trees have strong, woody stems.
Shrubs have multiple stems and are generally taller than creepers.
Creepers have weak stems and grow along the ground, spreading horizontally.
Climbers have weak stems but grow upwards with support.

questions.explanation: Creepers have weak stems and grow along the ground, spreading horizontally.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which part of a plant helps to hold it firmly in the soil and absorbs water and nutrients?

options.explanation: Roots anchor the plant in the soil and are responsible for absorbing water and essential nutrients from the ground.
Stems support the plant and transport water and nutrients.
Leaves are responsible for photosynthesis.
Flowers are responsible for reproduction.

questions.explanation: Roots anchor the plant in the soil and are responsible for absorbing water and essential nutrients from the ground.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Identify the group that consists only of animals that lay eggs.

options.explanation: These animals give birth to live young.
Hens, snakes, and fish are all animals that reproduce by laying eggs.
These animals give birth to live young.
These animals give birth to live young.

questions.explanation: Hens, snakes, and fish are all animals that reproduce by laying eggs.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Look at the two statements: Statement 1: All birds can fly. Statement 2: Birds have wings and lay eggs. Which statement is correct?

options.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect because some birds like penguins and ostriches cannot fly.
Statement 2 is correct as birds are characterized by having wings and reproducing by laying eggs.
Statement 1 is incorrect because some birds like penguins and ostriches cannot fly.
Statement 2 is correct as birds are characterized by having wings and reproducing by laying eggs.

questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect because some birds like penguins and ostriches cannot fly. Statement 2 is correct as birds are characterized by having wings and reproducing by laying eggs.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which of these is a large body of freshwater, usually surrounded by land?

options.explanation: Oceans are vast bodies of saltwater.
A lake is typically a large inland body of freshwater.
Rivers are flowing bodies of water.
Ponds are smaller than lakes.

questions.explanation: A lake is typically a large inland body of freshwater.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: A squirrel likes to eat nuts and fruits. It is an example of an animal that eats:

options.explanation: Animals that eat other animals are called carnivores.
Animals that eat only plants (like nuts and fruits) are called herbivores. Squirrels are primarily herbivores.
Animals that eat both plants and animals are called omnivores.
Squirrels primarily eat nuts and fruits, not insects.

questions.explanation: Animals that eat only plants (like nuts and fruits) are called herbivores. Squirrels are primarily herbivores.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: My body is covered with feathers, and I have a beak. I can fly high in the sky. Who am I?

options.explanation: Fish have scales and fins, and live in water.
Insects have exoskeletons and multiple limbs.
Birds are known for having feathers, a beak, and the ability to fly (though not all birds fly).
Mammals have hair and produce milk for their young.

questions.explanation: Birds are known for having feathers, a beak, and the ability to fly (though not all birds fly).
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which of these is a natural home for a fish?

options.explanation: Nests are for birds.
Dens are for animals like lions.
Burrows are for animals like rabbits.
Fish live in water bodies. A pond is a natural water body where fish can live.

questions.explanation: Fish live in water bodies. A pond is a natural water body where fish can live.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which of these is a land animal?

options.explanation: Fish is a water animal.
Duck is a water animal.
Elephant is a land animal.
Dolphin is a water animal.

questions.explanation: Fish, duck, and dolphin are typically water animals or spend significant time in water, whereas an elephant lives on land.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which of these animals lays eggs?

options.explanation: Cow gives birth to live young.
Dog gives birth to live young.
Hen lays eggs.
Cat gives birth to live young.

questions.explanation: Cows, dogs, and cats are mammals that give birth to live young. A hen is a bird that lays eggs.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: What is one important thing that plants give us to live?

options.explanation: Stones are not given by plants.
Although water is essential, it's not the primary thing plants give us.
Plants provide us with oxygen through photosynthesis.
Plastic is not given by plants.

questions.explanation: While water is essential, plants primarily provide us with oxygen (air to breathe) through photosynthesis, which is crucial for survival. Stones and plastic are not given by plants.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which of these creatures has wings and can fly?

options.explanation: Rabbit does not have wings.
Snake does not have wings.
Butterfly has wings and can fly.
Horse does not have wings.

questions.explanation: Rabbits, snakes, and horses do not have wings and cannot fly. A butterfly is an insect with wings that flies.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: A fish lives in water. Where does a monkey mostly live?

options.explanation: Desert is not a typical habitat for monkeys.
Monkeys primarily live in trees.
Snowy regions are not typical habitats for monkeys.
Monkeys do not live in ponds.

questions.explanation: Monkeys are arboreal animals, meaning they primarily live in trees in forests. Deserts and snowy regions are not their typical habitats, and while they might drink from a pond, they don't live in it.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which group contains only animals that eat plants?

options.explanation: These animals are carnivores.
These animals are herbivores.
Foxes and wolves are carnivores, and rabbits are herbivores but the group is mixed.
Dogs and cats are carnivores, and mice can be omnivores.

questions.explanation: Lions, tigers, bears, foxes, wolves, dogs, and cats are carnivores or omnivores. Cows, goats, and deer are herbivores, meaning they only eat plants.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: This animal has a very long neck and eats leaves from the tallest trees. Which animal is it?

options.explanation: Elephants have long trunks, not necks.
Zebras have short necks.
Giraffes have long necks to eat leaves from tall trees.
Crocodiles are reptiles with short necks.

questions.explanation: The description of having a very long neck to eat leaves from tall trees perfectly matches a giraffe. Elephants have long trunks, zebras have short necks, and crocodiles are reptiles with short necks.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a part of a plant?

options.explanation: Root is a part of a plant.
Stem is a part of a plant.
Leaf is a part of a plant.
Fin is not a part of a plant, it's found on fish.

questions.explanation: Roots, stems, and leaves are all essential parts of a plant. A fin is a body part found on fish and other aquatic animals, used for movement.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Rohan saw a small creature with six legs and antennae flying near a flower. What could it be?

options.explanation: Birds have two legs.
Fish have fins.
Insects have six legs and antennae, and some can fly.
Snakes have no legs.

questions.explanation: The description of having six legs, antennae, and flying near a flower points to an insect (like a bee, butterfly, or ant with wings). Birds have two legs, fish have fins, and snakes have no legs.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Consider these two statements about animals: Statement 1: A lion is a wild animal. Statement 2: A lion eats grass. Which option is correct?

options.text: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false.
options.explanation: Lions are wild animals and do not eat grass.

options.text: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are true.
options.explanation: Statement 2 is false because lions do not eat grass.

options.text: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are false.
options.explanation: Statement 1 is true because lions are wild animals.

options.text: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true.
options.explanation: Statement 1 is true and Statement 2 is false.

questions.explanation: Statement 1 is true because lions live in the wild and are not domesticated. Statement 2 is false because lions are carnivores and eat meat, not grass.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which of the following is a living thing?

options.explanation: Stone is a non-living object.
Chair is a non-living object.
A tree is a living thing because it grows, reproduces, and responds to its environment.
Cloud is a non-living object.

questions.explanation: A tree is a living thing because it grows, reproduces, and responds to its environment, unlike non-living objects like stone, chair, or cloud.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which animal is known as the 'Ship of the Desert'?

options.explanation: Elephants are not typically found in deserts.
Camels are well-adapted to desert life and can travel long distances without water.
Lions are not typically found in deserts.
Giraffes are not typically found in deserts.

questions.explanation: Camels are called the 'Ship of the Desert' because they are well-adapted to desert life and can travel long distances without water.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Assertion (A): Plants need sunlight to prepare their food. Reason (R): Plants prepare food through a process called photosynthesis.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

questions.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion. Plants use sunlight during photosynthesis to make their food.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Observe the image of a bird with a long beak and legs. Which habitat is it most likely to be found in?

options.explanation: Birds with long beaks and legs are not typically found in forests.
Birds with long beaks and legs are not typically found in deserts.
Birds with long beaks and legs are typically found in wetlands, where they can wade through water to catch fish or other prey.
Birds with long beaks and legs are not typically found in mountains.

questions.explanation: Birds with long beaks and legs are typically found in wetlands, where they can wade through water to catch fish or other prey.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which of the following helps a camel survive in the desert?

options.explanation: Thick fur would not help a camel survive in the desert.
While long eyelashes do help, they are not the only feature that helps a camel survive in the desert.
While wide feet do help, they are not the only feature that helps a camel survive in the desert.
Camels have long eyelashes to protect their eyes from sand and wide feet to walk on sand without sinking. Both features help them survive in the desert.

questions.explanation: Camels have long eyelashes to protect their eyes from sand and wide feet to walk on sand without sinking. Both features help them survive in the desert.
